match.reason: The closest bank point, phys-work-energy, covers W = Fs for a constant force but not the area under a force-distance graph, which the new point requires, and it is framed around energy at a Units 1 and 2 depth, so no bank point teaches this idea as it is needed.

draft.title: Work done by a force
card: Work is the energy transferred when a force moves an object. For a force along the direction of motion, W = Fs, where F is the force in newtons and s is the displacement in metres. Work is measured in joules.
If the force is at an angle to the motion, only the part of the force along the displacement does work. That part is F cos θ, so W = Fs cos θ.
On a force-distance graph, the work done is the area under the line. This works even when the force changes.
A force at right angles to the motion does no work. Work is positive if the force acts along the motion and negative if it acts against it.
draft.remember: Work is the force along the motion times the distance moved, or the area under a force-distance graph.

a.q: Which force does no work on the object?
opts: A satellite's weight while it moves in a circular orbit
A person's push on a trolley moving away from them
A rope pulling a sled forwards along flat snow
A brake pad's friction on a spinning wheel
a.why: In a circular orbit the weight acts towards the centre, at right angles to the motion, so it does no work. The other forces act along or against the motion, so they do work.
a.clue: Look for the force at right angles to the motion.

b.q: Priya pulls a suitcase 20 m along a flat floor. She pulls with a force of 50 N on a handle at 60° above the horizontal. How much work does she do on the suitcase?
b.why: Only the part of the force along the floor does work: W = 50 × 20 × cos 60° = 500 J. Using the full 50 N gives 1000 J, which wrongly counts the upward part of the pull.
b.clue: Find the part of the force that points along the motion.

a.best: A satellite's weight while it moves in a circular orbit
